UPSC Photo and Signature Size

UPSC application and registration screens set ranges for the photograph and signature images. Use these presets and then confirm the numbers against the instructions on the portal.

Size ranges last reviewed: 2026-10-04. Always confirm against your exam notification.

Compression tool

Target size Target size:
Exam range: Targets sit a little below the maximum. Check your notice.
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

What UPSC asks for

Requirements change with every notification. The ranges on this page are figures commonly reported for recent 2026 notices by exam-preparation websites, and the sources do not always agree. We have not verified them against each official PDF, so always follow the notification or instructions on the official application portal for your exam.

Reports of recent UPSC guidance describe a colour passport-size photograph in JPG format of roughly 20–200 KB, and a signature image of roughly 20–100 KB with a width of about 350–500 pixels. One source quotes up to 300 KB for the photograph, which shows how figures vary. Reports also mention live photograph capture and a signature image that contains three signatures in black ink.

Photograph preparation

Use a recent, clear colour photograph with a plain background and your face filling most of the frame, as the instructions describe. Crop to the required shape first, then use the Photo 20–200 KB preset here. The target of 190 KB leaves a margin under 200 KB.

Signature preparation

If your instructions ask for several signatures in one image, sign with a dark pen on plain white paper, leave space between the signatures, and photograph the sheet evenly. Crop around them and run the Signature 20–100 KB preset. The result card shows size and dimensions so you can compare them to the stated width range.

File names and format

Some instructions ask you to name files in a particular way. Rename the downloaded file after compression, and make sure the extension matches the real format. Renaming a PNG to .jpg does not convert it; use JPEG output here so the file is genuinely a JPEG.

Minimum size

UPSC ranges have a minimum as well as a maximum. A very simple image can fall under the minimum even at high quality. The tool will show a warning if that happens. In that case, use a higher-resolution original or keep more of the surrounding paper in the crop.

Keep one consistent signature

Your uploaded signature may be compared with what you sign later in the process. Practise the style you upload and use it consistently, as the official instructions advise.

Quick checklist

Confirm the current range on the portal, crop the photograph to the required shape, prepare the signature sheet on plain white paper, compress each file with its own preset, check the minimum as well as the maximum, name the files as instructed, and save a copy of everything you submit. Because live photograph matching may be part of the process, use a recent photograph that looks like you now, taken in good light, and avoid heavy filters or editing of the face.

Common questions

Is it 200 KB or 300 KB for the photo?

Sources differ and it can change by notice. Read the limit on the upload screen. If unsure, stay well under the lower figure.

Does this tool create three signatures in one image?

No. It only compresses and resizes an image you provide. Prepare the signatures on paper first, then photograph the whole sheet and crop it before compressing.

What if my signature file is under 20 KB?

Then it is below the usual minimum for this range. Photograph the sheet larger or sharper, crop with a little more margin, and run it again.
